text: 1. A non-transitory computer readable medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of modeling relationships between a plurality of e-mail users comprising: extracting a record of e-mail exchanges between the plurality of users, wherein the record is extracted from a database of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users, wherein the data is extracted through a direct internet access protocol; filtering the record to produce relevant interaction data based on the e-mail exchanges between the plurality of users, wherein the relevant interaction data includes a number of e-mail exchanges between each pair of the plurality of users; loading the relevant interaction data into a relationship modeling program, wherein the relationship modeling program assigns a weight to each of a plurality of characteristics of the relevant interaction data for each pair of the plurality of users, the plurality of characteristics comprising a time since a first interaction, a time since a last interaction, interaction volume between the two users, and a ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions, wherein the plurality of characteristics are further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone, wherein the relationship modeling program provides a model of relationships between each pair of the plurality of e-mail users by determining a relationship strength between each pair of the plurality of e-mail users based at least in part on the weight assigned to each of the plurality of characteristics; and displaying the model of relationships on a user interface.
2. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 further comprising populating an interaction database by monitoring e-mail exchanges and extracting relevant e-mail exchanges.

3. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein a characteristic of the plurality of characteristics is selected from a group consisting of interaction frequency, interaction type, number of communication participants.
4. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the plurality of characteristics comprises a time between interactions.

5. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the plurality of users is obtained from an e-mail field selected from a group consisting of SMTP, IMAP4, POP3, MIME, RFC 2046, RFC 2822, RFC 3156, and RFC 5322.

6. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the plurality of users of the e-mail system is obtained from a mail server, mail archives, and a log file.

7. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the plurality of users of the e-mail system is obtained from a spam filtering system based e-mail headers.

8. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the model of relationship includes strength of the relationship based on intimacy of conversations, frequency of communications, and historical age of the relationship.

9. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 1 , wherein the interaction data is further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone.

10. A method of processing relationship data in a server, the method comprising: receiving, at the server, data comprising a plurality of characteristics of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users of an e-mail system, wherein the data is transferred to the server from an interaction database of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users of the email system, and wherein the interaction database is populated through a direct internet access protocol, wherein the plurality of characteristics comprise a time since a first interaction, a time since a last interaction, interaction volume between the pair of users, and a ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions, and the plurality of characteristics are further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone; assigning a weight to each of the plurality of characteristics for each pair of users; transferring, from the server, the data to a processor for generating relationship data by determining a relationship strength associated with each pair of users; and displaying the relationship data on a user interface.

11. The method of claim 10 , wherein the displaying of the relationship data on the user interface comprises providing a graphical representation of the relationship strength associated with each pair of.
12. The method of claim 10 , wherein the interaction database is populated by monitoring e-mail exchanges and extracting relevant e-mail exchanges.
13. The method of claim 10 , wherein the characteristic comprises at least one selected from a group consisting of interaction frequency, interaction type, and number of communication participants.
14. The method of claim 10 , wherein the characteristic comprises a time between interactions.

15. The method of claim 10 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the pairs of users of the e-mail system is obtained from an e-mail field selected from a group consisting of SMTP, IMAP4, POP3, MIME, RFC 2046, RFC 2822, RFC 3156, and RFC 5322.
16. The method of claim 10 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the pairs of users of the e-mail system is obtained from a mail server, mail archives, and a log file.
17. The method of claim 10 , wherein the data associated with the e-mail exchanges between the pairs of users of the e-mail system is obtained from a spam filtering system based e-mail headers.
18. The method of claim 10 , wherein the strength of the relationship is based on intimacy of conversations, frequency of communications, and historical age of the relationship.

19. The method of claim 10 , wherein the characteristic of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users is further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone.

20. A non-transitory computer readable medium containing executable instructions that when executed perform a method of generating relationship data, comprising: accessing an interaction database of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users of an e-mail system; obtaining a plurality of characteristics of e-mail exchanges between the pairs of users and wherein the plurality of characteristics of e-mail exchanges fare further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone, wherein the plurality of characteristics are stored in the interaction database and wherein the data is obtained through a direct internet access protocol, wherein the plurality of characteristics comprise a time since a first interaction, a time since a last interaction, interaction volume between the pair of users, and a ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions; assigning a weight to each of the plurality of characteristics for each pair of users; generating relationship data by determining a relationship strength of associated with each pair of users based on the weight assigned to each of the plurality of characteristics for each pair of users; and displaying the relationship data on a user interface.

21. A system for processing relationship data, the system comprising: an e-mail system; an interaction database of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users of the e-mail system; a server to: receive data comprising a plurality of characteristics of e-mail exchanges between pairs of users of the e-mail system, wherein the data is transferred to the server from the interaction database, and wherein the interaction database is populated through a direct internet access protocol, wherein the plurality of characteristics comprise a time since a first interaction, a time since a last interaction, interaction volume between the pair of users, and a ratio of source to target versus target to source interactions, and the plurality of characteristics are further associated with at least one other digital communication medium selected from a group consisting of calendar, instant messaging, SMS, and phone; assign a weight to each of the plurality of characteristics for each pair of users; and transfer the data to a processor for generating relationship data by determining a relationship strength associated with each pair of users; and a user interface to display the relationship data.
